messages:
pagerduty-bot: PAGER DUTY — High error rate and request timeouts observed on /v2/generate (prod). Trigger: 4xx/5xx spike + latency > 8s. Paging @alex @maria @sree :rotating_light:

alex: taking this — switching my phone to DND then will DM for handoff if needed. grabbing logs now.

maria: on in 2m if you need backup. any immediate mitigation we can try?

sree: looking at metrics — GPUs in pool 'dedicated-gpu-pool-a' show 100% allocation, queue depth spiked. HPA didn't scale compute as expected.

jonathan_s: adding quick customer-impact note: CS reports degraded generation for 6 customers in EU region, average failure rate 42% for 10:40–10:58 UTC.

alex: timeline so far (rough): 10:37 UTC first small latency blip, 10:41 big spike, 10:43 alerts. Confirmed: many requests time out 30s, some 503s.

catalina: posting relevant graphs: (link) queue depth, GPU utilization, HPA events.

alex: sharing raw diagnostic snippet from runtime logs (cut):
```
2024-07-31T10:42:13Z runtime: enqueue req id=0x7f3fd depth=1200 model=llama-70b variant=q4_0
2024-07-31T10:42:14Z serving: allocate gpu=gpu-23 pool=dedicated-gpu-pool-a status=full
2024-07-31T10:42:15Z hpa: metric queue_depth=1180 target=200 replicas=12
2024-07-31T10:42:45Z runtime: warmup start model=llama-70b node=gke-node-07
2024-07-31T10:43:35Z runtime: warmup complete elapsed=90.4s
2024-07-31T10:44:00Z request id=0x7f3fd status=timeout
```

maria: warmup 90s is big — if HPA spins up nodes but GPUs are cold, requests pile up. Hypothesis A: scaling actions are starting nodes but model warmup/initialization is dominating latency so HPA doesn't reduce queue in time.

kevin: Hypothesis B: HPA threshold uses CPU load and not queue depth/latency; spikes didn't trigger HPA fast enough because CPU metric lagged.

ops-bot: HPA event stream pasted: replicas increased from 8 -> 12 at 10:42:30, then ->16 at 10:45:50. Pod readiness lag avg=75s.

alex: immediate mitigations attempted: 1) routed small-LLM fallback for non-SLA tenants (rolled at 10:46) — reduced failures for low-priority traffic. 2) manually increased GPU pool scaling target + cleared cold cache for a subset at 10:50.

jonathan_s: customer impact table (quick):
- tenant A: 68% errors 10:41–10:49
- tenant B: 34% errors 10:42–10:47
- tenant C: 0% (on Dedicated reserved lanes)

catalina: logs from autoscaler controller: ``events: scaling triggered by metric "queue_depth" but tolerance=0.2, change missed due to smoothing window=60s``

alex: collected kubectl outputs — `kubectl describe hpa inference-api` snippet:
```
Name: inference-api
Metrics: queue_depth (external) target 200 current 1120
Min replicas: 8, Max replicas: 32
Last scale time: 2024-07-31T10:42:30Z
Behavior: stabilization window up 60s
```

maria: can we confirm what triggers autoscale from the control plane? is it queue_depth directly or derived CPU? If it's derived, we should change to queue_depth fast path.

sree: checked autoscaler code — weight on CPU + smoothed queue. It will not jump aggressively due to 60s stabilization. That aligns with observed delay.

kevin: another datapoint — GPU pool reports show 0 warm spare GPUs at 10:41; pool autoscaler configured to maintain 0 warm spare for cost reasons. So when nodes spin up, no warmed model copies are available.

alex: putting down hypotheses list in-thread for postmortem: [H1] HPA stabilization window too long + CPU-weighted metric = slow reaction. [H2] No warm-spare GPUs / insufficient warm model preloading. [H3] Model warmup duration (70–100s) too long for current traffic burst profile. [H4] Fallback routing not applied to some tenant paths due to routing rule mismatch.

catalina: adding logs for a failed pod startup:
```
2024-07-31T10:43:00Z pod inference-pod-47 init: loading weights from /cache/model/llama-70b
2024-07-31T10:43:35Z pod inference-pod-47 init: weights extracted size=36GB elapsed=35s
2024-07-31T10:44:20Z pod inference-pod-47 runtime: kv-cache allocate 1.2GB elapsed=80s
```

alex: mitigation during incident summary: 10:46 route low-priority to small-llm; 10:50 increased pool target + kicked warmup for 4 nodes; 10:58 errors down to 6% for most tenants, full recovery 11:05.

maria: action items captured in-thread:
- Short-term (owners): reduce HPA stabilization window to 10s for queue_depth path (owner: sree) [ETA 48h]
- Mid-term: implement warm-spare pool with preloaded models for high-latency models (owner: kevin infra) [ETA 2w]
- Long-term: implement predictive pre-warming based on traffic spikes + waveform detection (owner: alex) [ETA roadmap]
- Postmortem: timeline & root cause writeup (owner: jonathan_s) [ETA 24h draft]

sree: I'll open the quick PR to change HPA behavior for the queue_depth metric in test env. will instrument canary.

kevin: infra will prototype a warm-spare node group with 2 preloaded GPUs for 70b-class models. cost evaluation incoming.

alex: tagging follow-ups: @product oncall for customer comms, @cs-team to confirm tenants impacted and outreach.

jonathan_s: I'll draft an initial incident summary for execs with timeline + mitigation steps. Will include the hypothesis list and logs above.

catalina: adding note — we should correlate this with last week's config change where we reduced warm spare to 0 (PR #2345). Might be a direct contributor.

alex: handoff: maria, you're on for next 2 hours to watch the canary metrics and confirm HPA changes. ping me if anything re-escalates.

maria: got it, monitoring dashboards. I'll post a short follow-up when the draft postmortem is up.

ops-bot: Incident closed (mitigated) at 1719982140. Summary: autoscaler reaction lag combined with no warm-spare GPUs and long model warmup caused queue amplification and request timeouts.

alex: thanks team. postmortem owner jonathan_s — please include cost tradeoffs for warm-spare and propose an SLO change if needed.

jonathan_s: will do — first draft by EOD UTC.

kevin: adding one more quick log snippet for posterity: `gpu-pool: scaleup start 10:42:20 target_gpus=8 -> 16; time_to_ready=220s due to node spinup + kube-provisioner delay`

maria: follow-up 24h: we saw a second smaller spike but HPA change held and warm-spare prototype reduced errors by ~60% in the canary cluster.

alex: closing thread — will move this into postmortem doc once jonathan posts. thanks all. :pray:
